title: Speed up the launcher's fingerprint-tests stage (10–14 min on Windows) by sharing immutable Git/worktree fixtures
outcome: Greg asked how to safely shorten gate time. Kimi::Consultant's measurement on Central FULL test-1397710a found the fingerprint-tests stage takes 10–14 min on Windows. By file: test-launcher.test 584.9s, commit-input 187.1s, ui-bootstrap 113.1s, git-path 98.6s, review-freeze-fingerprint 89.0s. The common cost is repeated real repository, worktree, toolchain and process setup, not assertion count. The slowest single tests run 17–20s each: info/exclude, clean commit, LF/CRLF, linked worktree bootstrap, MAX_PATH. The stage gets shorter by sharing immutable fixtures or using lighter process boundaries, with every behavior still checked.
acceptance: Before and after durations of the fingerprint-tests stage and of its five slowest files are recorded from launcher results on the same host. The stage is materially shorter on Windows.

Every existing assertion and behavior is still checked. Tests share only immutable fixtures (built once, never mutated by a test), or replace a heavy process boundary with a lighter one that exercises the same behavior. There are no deletions of behavioral coverage, no skips, no retries, no timeout changes, and no blanket parallelization that weakens isolation.
The independent review pair has no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding, and the full gate passes on the exact committed input on Windows and one other host.

completion.summary: Immutable private Git fixture seed delivered on master/origin in combo16, preserving custom-environment construction and every behavioral witness; observed same-host Windows stage10.466% shorter, with disclosed interference limitation. Fresh combined pair noMedium+, exact final tree FULL PASS on Windows B and DL560.
